name: StrixDB
tagline: Small Windows RDF store with SPARQL, SPARQL/Update and Datalog rule inference, embeddable via Lua or DLL.
description: StrixDB is Olivier Poirel's RDF store for medium-sized graphs, built on the GigaBASE embedded database for ACID storage. It answers SPARQL 1.0 queries and SPARQL/Update, adds Datalog-style rules (including recursion and negation) that can be applied inside SPARQL queries for reasoning such as OWL property rules, and reads and writes RDF/XML and Turtle. You can use it as a Lua module, as a Windows DLL from C, C++ or Java, or as an Apache httpd module that serves the SPARQL protocol. It is free but closed-source and 32-bit Windows only, and the last release, 0.94.5, dates from April 2011, so it suits experiments more than production.
statusNote: Downloads remain online, but the last release was 0.94.5 (April 2011) and the project is dormant. Apache Jena or RDF4J are maintained alternatives.

scale.notes: 32-bit builds limit triple and resource IDs to 2^32.

strengths: Datalog rules with recursion and negation usable directly inside SPARQL
Several deployment modes: Lua module, DLL or SPARQL endpoint behind Apache
ACID storage on GigaBASE for a small footprint
weaknesses: No release since 2011 and no SPARQL 1.1
Sized for medium graphs, not billions of triples
useCases: Experimenting with rule-based reasoning over small RDF graphs
